original_question: Classify projective contact manifolds: is every projective contact manifold either the projectivized cotangent bundle P(T^*M) of a compact complex manifold M or the closed contact Fano orbit X_g associated with a simple complex Lie algebra g?
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("Compact contact manifolds"), Conjecture 6, together with the paper's explicit rephrasing as Conjecture 7. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct conjectural classification problem: it asks about projective contact manifolds, names exactly the two model families listed in the paper, and phrases the issue as an exhaustive either/or classification. That is very close to the paper's actual target, namely Conjecture 6 in Section 4. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is entirely in the complex holomorphic setting: X is a complex manifold, not a real contact manifold or a variety over an unspecified field. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

A contact structure is not left implicit in the paper: X has odd complex dimension 2r+1 and carries a twisted 1-form theta in H^0(X, Omega^1_X ⊗ L) for some line bundle L such that theta ∧ (d theta)^r is nowhere zero. Your draft assumes this notion but does not state it. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

The second class is described more precisely in the paper: for a simple complex Lie algebra g, X_g is the unique closed orbit of the adjoint group acting on P(g), and X_g is a contact Fano manifold. Your draft names X_g but does not spell out this construction. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

The quantifier is universal and unconditional: the conjecture asks whether every projective contact manifold falls into one of those two classes, with no extra hypotheses such as Fano, Picard number 1, or homogeneity assumed at the outset. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))

The nearby context adds an explicit equivalent reformulation used by the paper itself: because a projective contact manifold is either of type PT^*M or Fano with b_2 = 1, and a homogeneous Fano contact manifold is of type X_g, the conjecture is rephrased as Conjecture 7. This reduction is not visible from your draft alone. ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a projective complex manifold of odd dimension 2r+1 endowed with a holomorphic contact structure, i.e. a twisted 1-form theta in H^0(X, Omega^1_X ⊗ L) for some line bundle L such that theta ∧ (d theta)^r is nowhere vanishing. Must X be either the projective cotangent bundle PT^*M of a compact complex manifold M, or the unique closed adjoint-group orbit X_g contained in P(g) for some simple complex Lie algebra g? ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, as the paper explicitly rephrases the problem after recalling the partial classification result: is every contact Fano manifold homogeneous? ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
justification: The introduction says that the contact part of the paper is devoted to the conjectural classification of projective contact manifolds, which already identifies the relevant target section. Section 4 then states exactly the classification conjecture your draft is aiming at: "Any projective contact manifold is of type a) or b)." The next paragraph explains why the author can rephrase this as "A contact Fano manifold is homogeneous." Hence your draft is essentially on target, but to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful it needs the complex-holomorphic definition of a contact structure and the precise description of X_g as the unique closed adjoint orbit in P(g). ([nzdr.ru](https://nzdr.ru/data/media/biblio/kolxoz/M/MD/MDdg/Ebeling%20W.%2C%20Hulek%20K.%2C%20Smoczyk%20K.%20%28eds.%29%20Complex%20and%20differential%20geometry%20%28Springer%2C%202011%29%28ISBN%203642202993%29%28O%29%28431s%29_MDdg_.pdf))
